prompt: Reformat sloppily indented Java source the way an IDE's auto-indent does, using brace depth. Complete SourceBlockIndenter, then run the tests.
explanation: Auto-indent is a one-pass state machine: the depth counter carries across lines, and each line is printed at the depth that was in force before its own braces are applied. The special case is a line that begins with '}' -- it closes a block it did not open, so it is printed one level out while every other line uses the running depth. Passing -1 to split keeps trailing empty lines instead of silently dropping them, and clamping the level and the depth at 0 keeps stray closing braces from producing negative indents.
hints: source.split("\n", -1) keeps trailing empty lines; join the result back with "\n" as you build it.
Decide the line's indent level BEFORE updating depth, and only the leading-'}' case uses depth - 1.
"    ".repeat(level) builds the indent; then depth += (number of '{') - (number of '}') for the next line.
